title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues item 7 from the previous page, on the complex 'Teichmüller towers'. In the notation there, M_{g,ν} (calligraphic or tilde) is the universal cover of the moduli orbifold M^an_{g,ν}, i.e. Teichmüller space. T_{g,ν} is the Teichmüller modular group, i.e. the mapping class group Γ_{g,ν}.

1. Grothendieck records that Teichmüller did not define an interesting intrinsic Riemannian metric on Teichmüller space, only Finsler metrics. This is the Teichmüller metric, which is Finsler and, by Masur's work, not non-positively curved.

2. One would like a complete Riemannian metric of negative curvature. Then Cartan's fixed point theorem, resting on existence and uniqueness of the geodesic joining two points, would give a simple geometric proof that every finite group of complex automorphisms of Teichmüller space has a fixed point. In particular every finite subgroup of the mapping class group would fix a point. Equivalently, the subgroup is realised as a group of automorphisms of some marked Riemann surface: this is the Nielsen realization problem.

3. The marginal figure sketches an averaging mechanism for a cyclic group <g>. Take x0 and its orbit, form the geodesic polygon x0, gx0, g²x0, …. Let x1 be the midpoint of x0 and gx0; its orbit gives a new polygon, then x2, and so on. The iteration should converge to a 'pt fixe par moyennisation' at the centre. In CAT(0) geometry one gets d(x_{k+1}, g x_{k+1}) ≤ d(x_k, g x_k). Cartan's own argument is cleaner: take the circumcentre of a bounded orbit.

4. Deligne's opinion is reported: he believes it is true that every finite subgroup of T_{g,ν} has a fixed point in Teichmüller space. However, he does not find this route via a negatively curved Riemannian metric plausible.

5. Item 8 is gossip and references:
- Mumford would know a presentation of the T_{g,ν} in terms of the usual (Dehn twist) generators.
- L. Bers (Columbia) works on complex Teichmüller theory and uses it to study compactifications of the M_{g,ν}.

The page serves Grothendieck's anabelian/Teichmüller-tower program. Torsion in the Teichmüller groups corresponds to curves with automorphisms, i.e. orbifold points of the moduli stack. Knowing that finite subgroups are exactly stabilisers is needed to control finite subgroups and their conjugacy classes in π1 of the moduli stack and in its profinite completion with Galois action.
errors: No mathematical error. The idea is sound in principle, but there is a historical gap: the statement Grothendieck and Deligne treat as conjectural was already proved. Kerckhoff solved the Nielsen realization problem (announced in Bull. AMS 1980, published in Annals 1983) using convexity of length functions along earthquake paths. Grothendieck appears unaware of this.

The hoped-for metric exists only partially. The Weil–Petersson metric is Riemannian (Kähler) with negative sectional curvature (Wolpert, Tromba, c. 1986), but it is incomplete. Cartan's theorem therefore cannot be applied naively: a fixed point of the completion could lie on the boundary. Wolpert (1987) nevertheless proved Nielsen realization via Weil–Petersson geodesic convexity of length functions. Later, CAT(0)-ness of the completion (Yamada, Wolpert, Daskalopoulos–Wentworth) plus a stratum argument recovers the Cartan-style proof. So Deligne's scepticism was not borne out.

The midpoint-iteration sketch does not by itself guarantee convergence. Displacement is non-increasing in CAT(0) space, but strict contraction needs an argument; the circumcentre argument is the standard rigorous route.

ideas.what: Use a complete negatively curved Riemannian metric on Teichmüller space plus Cartan's fixed point theorem to show finite subgroups of the mapping class group have fixed points.
ideas.modern_name: Nielsen realization problem; Weil–Petersson convexity / CAT(0) approach
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kerckhoff 1980/83 (earthquakes); Wolpert 1987 (Weil–Petersson convexity); Cartan fixed point theorem (1920s); Bruhat–Tits
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses finite subgroups of Teichmüller groups in the tower context; this specific metric argument is not known to be there.

ideas.what: Fixed point by iterated averaging (midpoint polygons) of an orbit of a cyclic group.
ideas.modern_name: Barycentre/circumcentre fixed-point arguments in CAT(0) spaces

ideas.what: Teichmüller's metric is Finsler, not Riemannian.
Presentation of mapping class groups via standard generators; Bers' compactification.

missed.claim: A historical datum: in 1981, Grothendieck (reporting Deligne) treated Nielsen realization as open and hoped for a negatively curved Riemannian metric to prove it via Cartan. This is exactly the route Wolpert took a few years later with Weil–Petersson, against Deligne's reported scepticism. It is not a new result; it documents the state of knowledge in the Grothendieck–Deligne circle.
missed.quote: On aurait voulu trouver une métrique riemannienne à courbure négative, qui permettrait donc par un argument géométrique simple (Cartan) ... de prouver que tout groupe fini d'automorph. complexes de M_{g,ν} admet un pt fixe.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest only: it shows the anabelian program's need for Nielsen realization and the transmission gap with Kerckhoff's work.

deep.surprise_reason: The ideas (Cartan fixed-point approach to Nielsen realization, Finsler versus Riemannian metrics on Teichmüller space) are standard and were carried out by Kerckhoff and Wolpert. The page is mainly a historical snapshot showing Grothendieck and Deligne apparently unaware of Kerckhoff's solution.
transcription_corrections: The first line likely begins with '[Teichmüller] n'a pas défini par là de métrique riemannienne intrinsèque intéressante'.
'Deligne veut que c'est vrai que' is more plausibly 'Deligne pense que c'est vrai que' (reading uncertain).

In the figure, the points x1, x2 are successive midpoints (x1 between x0 and gx0, x2 between x1 and gx1), illustrating a fixed point obtained by averaging; the label reads 'pt fixe par moyennisation'.
In this note M_{g,ν} denotes Teichmüller space (the universal cover), not the moduli space, and T_{g,ν} denotes the Teichmüller modular (mapping class) group.
